problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(3,1,5),\,B(6,-8,0)$, and $C(-2,1,3).$

feedback.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $P(7,-3,4)$ and $Q(5,1,-1),$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨\sqrt{5},-3,2⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). We already have one vector $v=⟨\sqrt{5},-3,2⟩.$ Let's also use the displacement vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨5,1,-1⟩-⟨7,-3,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,4,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $p=⟨7,-3,4⟩$ of the point $P,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+sv+t\overset{\to }{PQ} \\ r & =⟨7,-3,4⟩+s⟨\sqrt{5},-3,2⟩+t⟨-2,4,-5⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
